_doc: MISSOURI MEERSCHAUM dating cabinet (#38, Wave E, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #44). The corncob house of Washington, Missouri — world's oldest+largest corncob maker. Mostly an IDENTIFICATION cabinet (cobs are consumables; few dated marks): the one hard cliff = the 1907 company rename H. Tibbe & Son -> Missouri Meerschaum Company. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Missouri_Meerschaum.json (+ Factory_Tour + Corncob_Buying_Guide mirrors, unmined -> future).

history_anchors._doc: 1869: Henry Tibbe (Dutch immigrant woodworker) begins turning corncob pipes in Washington, MO (the farmer-whittler legend). 1878: Tibbe patents the plaster-of-Paris bowl-coating process ('Missouri Meerschaum' coined — likening the porous cool smoke to Turkish meerschaum). Nationwide distribution follows; by 1925 ~a dozen corncob companies in Franklin County — Missouri Meerschaum is the sole survivor. 1907: H. TIBBE & SON CO becomes MISSOURI MEERSCHAUM COMPANY. Factory at 400 West Front Street (riverfront) since the early days; 1904 St. Louis World's Fair display (museum holds it). Famous smokers: Gen. Douglas MacArthur (the WWII icon — drove the postwar corncob boom; see also Tsuge history). College class pipes (1906 Harvard example known).

brand_marks.physical: Plaster-coated corncob bowls, wood or plastic (later) shanks/bits. Paper labels + stamps vary by era; most cobs carry little datable nomenclature — dating leans on construction details (bit material, band, label typography) not yet systematized.

H. Tibbe / H. Tibbe & Son marks = pre-1907
